chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas
paraphrase: Adult pancreas about 100 g and 14 to 23 cm long (cites ref 2, AFIP fascicle); size compared to half a hand.
note: Model has 12-15 cm: both books give a longer range. Gorelick says 14-23, Beger says 14-25.

chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas
paraphrase: Weight stated as roughly 100 grams.
note: Model range 80-100 g; books give a single approximate value of 100 g.

value: 14–25 cm; ~100 g; example specimen 22.5 cm (47-y woman autopsy)
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas
paraphrase: Same statement, upgraded to 14-25 cm; Fig 2.1 legend gives one dissected autopsy pancreas at 22.5 cm.
note: Beger 2023 is a revision of the Gorelick chapter (same author); not independent evidence.

chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas
paraphrase: Exocrine part (acini, ducts, connective tissue, vessels, nerves) is over 95% of the pancreas by mass.
note: Same sentence in Beger p.9. Includes ducts and stroma, not only acinar cells.

chapter: Hruban & Iacobuzio-Donahue, ch.19 The Pancreas (Robbins & Cotran 9th ed, Saunders 2015)
paraphrase: Exocrine pancreas said to make up 80-85% of the organ; acinar cells pyramidal; islets about a million.
note: Conflicts with >95% (different definition). Robbins is a pathology text; not primary data.

chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas
paraphrase: Islets make up 1 to 2 percent of the adult pancreas in most mammalian species.
note: Also p.3 (pdf 14) and Beger p.9, p.20.

parameter: pancreas tissue volume composition (acinar, duct, vessel, endocrine, matrix)

species: species NOT stated in chapter; ref [1] is Bolender 1974, a stereology paper on guinea pig pancreas (from the reference list)
chapter: Petersen OH, ch.4 Physiology of Acinar Cell Secretion
paraphrase: By volume the pancreas is mostly acinar cells (82%), with duct cells 4%, vessels 4%, endocrine 2%, matrix 8%.
note: Species is an inference from the cited reference (Bolender, J Cell Biol 1974, guinea pig); text does not say. Do not label human. Best available number for acinar % and duct %.

parameter: ductal cells as share of exocrine tissue

paraphrase: Exocrine part is over 95% of the gland; acinar cells most abundant, duct cells about a fifth of the exocrine tissue.
note: Conflicts with Petersen 4% duct by volume. Different metric (cell number vs volume?) and no citation shown for it. Needs primary source.

parameter: acinar cells as share of pancreatic epithelial cells

note: No primary citation at that sentence.

species: not stated (Ca2+ imaging literature; mostly mouse/rat)

value: up to several hundred

value: spherical, single membrane, in apical cytoplasm; variable number
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas

note: No count per cell given in any of the three books.

value: nuclei basal; Golgi at junction of basal and apical; RER abundant basal/perinuclear; mitochondria densest basal and central
chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas (Fig 17 legend)
paraphrase: Nuclei sit basally, Golgi between basal and apical zones, centroacinar cells have less RER and no granules.
note: Qualitative only. Many acinar cells binucleate (Beger p.13, evidence from rat, human significance unknown).

value: many
species: observation based on rat; human significance unknown
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas
paraphrase: Many acinar cells are binucleate; detailed characterization comes from rat tissue.
note: Model uses one nucleus; worth a note.

value: pale cytoplasm, no secretory granules, less RER, mitochondria numerous, microvilli; at acinus-ductule junction or inside acinar tubule
chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas
paraphrase: Centroacinar cells are smaller than acinar cells, granule-free, and sit at the junction of acinus and small ductule or among acinar cells.
note: No count per acinus and no size given. Model value 3 per acinus is NOT supported by these books.

value: acini and acinar tubules form an anastomosing network, not grape-like clusters
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas
paraphrase: Recent work shows acini and tubules form an anastomosing tubular network; an acinus may be a blind end or an intermediate segment.
note: Relevant to the project rule 'one intercalated duct per acinus ending at it': books say acini can also sit mid-tubule with ductules on both sides (Beger p.13).

value: main duct > interlobular > intralobular ducts > ductules (= intercalated); single layer of cuboidal cells; collagenous wall thick in main/interlobular, thin in small ducts, none in ductules
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas
paraphrase: Terminology: ductule equals intercalated duct; single cuboidal layer; wall of connective tissue thickens as ducts get larger; smallest ducts lack smooth muscle.
note: No diameters or cell heights stated anywhere. Pdf 33 (p.17) and Gorelick pdf 18-19, 22-23.

value: not given numerically
chapter: Longnecker DS & Thompson ED, ch.2 Anatomy, Histology, and Fine Structure of the Pancreas
paraphrase: Duct cells are cuboidal, single-nucleus, with less cytoplasm than acinar cells; no dimensions.
note: Model values (outer radius 5, 12, 26-45 µm; cell heights 3, 6 µm) remain unsourced.

value: head 2.4, body 1.8, tail 1.2
chapter: Irisawa A & Yamamiya A, ch.43 Abdominal Imaging for the Diagnosis of Chronic Pancreatitis (EUS section)
paraphrase: On EUS the normal main duct measures about 2.4 mm in the head, 1.8 mm in the body and 1.2 mm in the tail (cites ref 38).
note: Imaging measurement of lumen, not outer duct radius. Rosemont minor criterion: dilated if body >=3.5 mm, tail >1.5 mm. Model 'several mm' is consistent but main duct is ~1-2.5 mm, not several.

value: ~70% between 50 and 250; average 100–150

note: Model mean ~110 µm is slightly below the stated average range. Cites ref 4 in the chapter (Pancreapedia).

value: same as above

species: not stated (general; cites Pan & Wright 2011, Edlund 2002, Bonner-Weir 2015)

value: human 5–10; mouse 2–5
chapter: Golson ML, ch.6 Pancreatic delta cells: an overlooked cell in focus
paraphrase: Delta cells are 5-10% of adult human islets (Wang 2016) and 2-5% of mouse islets.
note: Conflicts slightly with Longnecker ~5%. Delta cells interspersed in human islets.

value: ~9–10 (average)
chapter: Golson ML, ch.6
paraphrase: Alpha and beta cells average around 9-10 µm across; delta cells have 5-30 µm axon-like projections (Arrojo 2019).
note: Model islet cell diameter is 11 µm; this suggests 9-10. Delta cell body size not given.

paraphrase: Stellate cells make up about 4-7% of parenchymal cells in normal pancreas and sit around basolateral aspects of acini, vessels, small ducts, islets.
note: Good match for a number. Species unspecified.

value: thin periacinar cells with extensions between acinar cells; lipid/vitamin A droplets; no size
chapter: Longnecker DS, ch.1 Anatomy and histology of the pancreas (Fig 29 legend)
paraphrase: A stellate cell lies in the interstitium with a cytoplasmic process pushing between two acinar cells; dark inclusions probably lipid droplets.
note: No dimensions in any of the three books. Beger p.35 Fig 2.17-2.18 same and Petersen p.49 calls them 'very thin periacinar cells'.

value: each acinus supplied by capillary plexus; intralobular arteries run parallel to ducts; islet capillaries connect to acinar capillaries
chapter: Hadley SM & Gardner TB, ch.24 Conservative Therapy of Acute Pancreatitis
paraphrase: Intralobular arteries, often alongside ducts, feed a lobular capillary plexus that supplies the acinus; capillary flow is biased toward islet cells.
note: No capillary diameter or distance. Beger p.21 describes insulo-acinar portal arrangement (acinar cells near islets larger, more zymogen).

value: about 1
chapter: Owyang C & DiMagno MJ, ch.7 Neurohormonal and Hormonal Control of Pancreatic Secretion
paraphrase: The human pancreas secretes about one litre of juice per day, mostly water, electrolytes and digestive enzymes.
note: Only one book gives a number; no enzyme output figure found. Ducts supply bulk of volume, acinar fluid small (Beger p.48, pdf 62).

value: acinar cells secrete a small volume of NaCl-rich fluid; ducts secrete bulk (HCO3- rich)
chapter: Lin W-Y, Sarkar P, Muallem S, ch.5 Physiology of Duct Cell Secretion
paraphrase: Two-step process: small acinar volume, ducts add the bulk of the fluid.
